speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; to begin our evaluation, have you ever experienced fractures from minor trauma or falls from standing height?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Calcium, Phosphate, ALP, PTH, 25-OH Vitamin D, IGF-1, and Karyotype.
REQUEST IMAGES: Hand_and_Wrist_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mention of "Tuberculosis" is clearly incorrect given your history of delayed menarche, clitoromegaly, and bone fragility; please ignore that advice. To better understand your condition, did you experience short stature or have your growth plates close early?

REQUEST TEST: TSH, T4, Cortisol, ACTH, LH, FSH, Testosterone, DHEA-S, 17-OHP, and 24-hour Urine Free Cortisol.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: Normal; T4: Normal; Cortisol: Normal; ACTH: Normal; LH: Elevated; FSH: Normal; Testosterone: Elevated; DHEA-S: Elevated; 17-OHP: Normal; 24-hour Urine Free Cortisol: Normal. Pelvic Ultrasound: Ovaries with multiple cysts and a normal uterus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH).

Your elevated testosterone, DHEA-S, and LH levels combined with normal cortisol and 17-OHP, along with your history of virilization and bone fragility, confirm a diagnosis of late-onset or non-classic CAH. The multiple ovarian cysts on your ultrasound are likely secondary to chronic hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology.

REQUEST TEST: 21-hydroxylase activity assay or genetic testing for CYP21A2 mutation.
